answers.answer: In London Season, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one to that card's roll for each fatigue on it, and add one more for the Chairman. A modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue to the card; 5 or higher retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: ‘Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card’; ‘Chairman also adds one’; retiree to Pensioners, card to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select a London Season display card, taking or discarding one apiece. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending. Ties go to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes; any remaining tie is resolved clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replenish cards during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players immediately. After the selection step, discard every card still displayed and refill the display with exactly three cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected one. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies; they do not carry over.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige and Retirements: eligible players, descending spending; windows then PM-clockwise tiebreakers; empty-display skip; discard/refill three; unused Pensioners returned.

answers.answer: At the start of the Family phase, check where your opportunity marker is. You may take your chosen main action twice only if the marker was already on that action at phase start; then place/move the marker onto the chosen main action. The latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action after the main action. That extra action is never doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer grants one additional writer once that turn. Since the marker already matches Enlist Writer, its main action can be taken twice, placing two writers, plus the once-per-turn vacancy bonus: three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family phase: marker checked at phase start; matching action may be taken twice; extra-action law is not doubled; Enlist Writer table row grants one additional writer once with at least four vacant offices.

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant from the Stock Exchange into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Court pieces are Company shares. If Debt is gone, slide any remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. A Seek Share action pays its listed purchase cost to the bank; it does not pay family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share and New Company shares: rightmost applicant moves to Court as Debt decreases; absent Debt applicants slide right; Seek Share never pays into Company treasuries.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the back of each office card. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that family member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. When promoting an officeholder, move that person's fatigue onto the new office card and put the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. Ordinary hiring of your own family's member requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If there is no eligible candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip that office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ascending number; promotion transfers fatigue and inserts old card; Nepotism paragraph; no candidate or vacant hirer means skip.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody gains the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without nepotism consent. The elected Chairman piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority calculations and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm; therefore it is not a tradable share.
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: pure majority, first supported candidate; former Chairman resolves no majority; piece still counts as share but cannot be traded or invested.

answers.answer: For a Company-office success check, first commit the needed resources and cash; cash must come from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Resolve using the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails, with a retry allowed only if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic failure. On catastrophe, the officeholder returns to supply, their fatigue is discarded, the office card is flipped into Vacant Offices, and that office takes no more actions. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify the general check. Do not take a dead action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: treasury payment to bank, lowest die outcomes, retry condition, catastrophe destinations and dead-action examples.

answers.answer: The Chairman may voluntarily add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance per Debt, without seeking consent. Each further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman's shares in that majority. Borrowing may never pass the end of the Debt track. The Chairman must then allocate all Company Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved as long as the borrowing limits are respected. Money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: ‘up to three Debt freely’; additional advance majority consent; never pass track end; allocate all Balance to other offices.

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury funds until £2 or less remains. For £2, lease an extra ship; for £3, fit a ship from a shipyard, without needing its owner's consent; for £5, buy a Company ship, but only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships serve only until Refresh. The stated shipyard-fit and lease actions do not require owner consent; the separate purchase-from-owner procedure is not part of the listed Shipping action.
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: budget limit, lease £2, fit £3 without owner consent, buy Company ship £5 only after shipyards are empty; any sea zone.

answers.answer: A President declares regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders within available ship capacity. Each £1 from that Presidency's treasury buys one die, and each declared nonhome region subtracts one die. A failed check may be retried during that President's operations if affordable; another position cannot act between that President's attempts. A President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. The first writer goes to the home port; every following order must be adjacent to one already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. No President may fill another President's home region, even if that other Presidency's office is vacant. Add each order's printed revenue to Company Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order; owners receive £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declared regions/dice penalty, retries and one-success limit, order route and capacity, home-region restriction, revenue and bonuses.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or a region bordering one of its associated regions. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for Deploy to have an effect. The Commander exhausts chosen officers and regiments for one die each, and local alliances for their printed dice. Subtract the strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, whether success, failure or catastrophe, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target limits and Company-region requirement; exhausted resources/dice; empire-strength penalty; after each attempt officer-loss dice.

answers.answer: On successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of one pound per surviving officer used in that attempt plus one. Distribute the available loot in repeating payout cycles: first the Commander gets £1 for themself plus £1 per used surviving officer of theirs; then, clockwise, other families get £1 per used surviving officer; finally the bank gets £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength. Stop a cycle when cash runs out, then repeat from the Commander until the loot is exhausted. Give the Commander one trophy per target tower. Impose control by removing the target tower/dome, removing all matching empire flags if it was a capital, opening its orders and clearing unrest. For a newly Company-controlled region, place its loot/control token region-side above the President. Place a Governor overlay in the conquered region and its office card in Vacant Offices; if the Elephant was there pointing outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member goes to supply; exhausted officers still undergo loss checks. There is no Commander office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: success loot formula, payout-cycle table, trophies and control steps; catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: A Governor begins with the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of the result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: Build Company ship, Commission regiment, or Tax. Build requires two successful Build choices: if there is no partially built ship in the region, place one there; otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. Commission a regiment into that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, has no dice left, or catastrophically fails.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer tables: shrinking pool, success cash/preceding failure bonus, options, tax unrest, failed roll and stopping conditions.

answers.answer: During Company Revenue, reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one per loan until the Debt track ends. Emergency loans continue even at maximum Debt, and newly added Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two. Next compare the remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if short, lower Standing one. Then the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, at one pound per Company share, paying each share owner—including the Chairman—£1 per share. If total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
answers.evidence: Revenue: expenses, emergency loans (including at maximum Debt), Standing losses, then Expectations and Dividends.

answers.answer: When an Invasion or Rebellion attacks a Company region, resolve the primary attack first. A normal primary Crisis uses the normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength plus unrest in its target region; a primary Foreign Invasion instead uses its ordinary attack die without added unrest. Then resolve secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency its Commander orders the attacks. Each secondary attack strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; use local alliances at their printed strength and do not split them. If newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, perform Region Loss. If sufficient, clear all unrest and give the Commander one trophy; if this successfully defends against a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and receives or loses no trophies. This does not appoint a Commander. A successful primary Invasion against the Company also applies empire growth.
answers.evidence: Events—Attacks on Company: primary then secondary order and attack strengths; defense and successful-defense results; vacant Commander substitute.

answers.answer: After voting, support of −1 or less means failure: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text if applicable, return the Opposition Leader token and give the PM dial to the Opposition Leader. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support of zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, and then resolve the law's immediate effects. In either outcome, restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. Thus exactly zero support passes, and only negative support fails.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Resolution: ‘−1 or less fails’; ‘Zero or higher passes’; failed-law PM/policy sequence; passed policy then immediate effects; card restoration.

answers.answer: In the 1758 and Long 1710 scenarios, the Prime Minister may call a special Deregulation vote at the start of a turn, before London Season, if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; the PM must call it if either track is on a starred space. Passing lowers Debt by one for every two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives the PM a passed-law token, and activates firms. Failing increases Company share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. This special law has no policy, so the ordinary policy selection/resolution does not apply; failure does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated. The 1710 scenario has no deregulation procedure per its setup description.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: scenario call conditions and timing; pass/fail consequences; ‘No policy accompanies this law’; failure exceptions; scenario table identifies 1813 start and 1710 without deregulation.

answers.answer: During the Firms phase, a player who currently manages no firm may form one by returning an eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to its invested side. Flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set Value to the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get its manager's consent and contribute a Company share or workshop in the same way; take £5 from the bank into London for each contribution. The Chairman's share is ineligible; Company shares cannot be used when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and shares created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. An invested workshop stays invested even if its firm fails and never earns the workshop bonus or Company-failure VP. Firms may have at most ten shares: contributions beyond that still add £5 but create no share.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Form a firm and Invest: eligibility, contribution and bank money; listed Company-share restrictions, permanent workshop status and ten-share cap.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose either a trade zone/home port or Hobnob. A trade strategy requires at least one ship and commits a secret cash bid from London; a closed home port is still allowed when selecting it. Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends, but the firm still pays expenses and keeps its previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously, keeping strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, firms reveal their strategies and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative; a President's successful Trade sets its initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After that successful President trade, fill in ascending initiative, with the President choosing among ties. If the President is vacant or never succeeds at Trade, firms fill after Commanders and Governors have had their chance, with the Chairman breaking initiative ties. Each firm fills as many open orders as possible, up to ships plus one, starting at its strategy home port and tracing a route through its own filled orders back there; it may fill each order only once. Firms can refill orders filled earlier that turn by others, and the Company can refill firm-filled orders. A previously filled order pays half its listed value, rounded down, instead of full revenue. Revenue goes to the firm's India treasury. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to that treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: one attempt, choices/reveals/checks and initiative; order-filling capacity/routes, repeat-fill revenue and value growth.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then the other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows, then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm's share count or Value. Pay from either or both firm treasuries. If the firm cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued: its shares go to Debtor's Prison (each costs −1 VP), ships return to shipyards, its charter returns to the family side, and invested workshops remain invested. Rescue may use emergency investments following normal contribution rules; even when the ten-share cap prevents new shares, the contribution pays expenses, remaining cash is lost, and Value drops one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, merge into one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not yet paid and cover the endangered firm's shortfall. After expenses, a manager may pay dividends only from India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares. Record the total actual cash paid out—not a per-share amount—on the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm that pays nothing records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: expense formula/source; dissolution destinations; rescue routes; dividends and marker treatment; workshop fate.
